skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through structured code reviews of changed files, with checks for OWASP Top 10 risks, SQLAlchemy ORM performance, bugs, and project standards.
skill.summary: Review changed files for security, performance, bugs, and project standards.
skill.author: DavidDworetzky

security_audit.summary: The high and critical static alerts in the reference markdown are false positives because they are example patterns and checklists, not executable payloads. The shell helper only runs fixed git commands, but the skill has medium-risk guidance to read author-specific absolute paths and to edit code without explicit approval. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Author-specific absolute paths in skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace absolute paths with relative project files, optional discovery steps, and an explicit request before reading outside the workspace.

remediation.issue: Review workflow instructs immediate code fixes.
remediation.suggestion: Separate review reporting from edits, and require explicit user approval before applying any changes.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Absolute Local File Access
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to read author-specific absolute paths under /Users/daviddworetzky/Documents/repos/Geist. This can cause unnecessary local file access outside the reviewed repository and fails on other machines.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file paths are explicit absolute local paths in the skill instructions. They are not prompt injection, but they are direct guidance to read files outside the portable skill context.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Code Modification Without Explicit Consent

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The action section directly says to fix issues immediately and show before and after code. The behavior is clear, although a user may still grant edit permissions in some sessions.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes for Security and Performance
content.value_statement: Manual code review can miss security, performance, and ORM issues in changed files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured review checks.
actual_capabilities: Finds changed files using git diff workflows.
Reviews code for OWASP Top 10 vulnerability patterns.
Checks SQLAlchemy code for N+1 queries and missing eager loading.
Flags logic bugs, error handling gaps, and edge cases.
Compares Python and backend changes against stated project standards.
Formats review results by severity with recommended fixes.
limitations: The guidance is strongest for Python, SQLAlchemy, and backend code.
Project standards paths are author-specific and may not exist elsewhere.
It does not run tests, linters, or dependency scanners by itself.
It depends on available git history and readable changed files.

use_cases.title: Pre-Commit Review
use_cases.description: Review staged and unstaged changes before committing to catch bugs, risky patterns, and missing standards checks.

use_cases.title: Backend Security Review
use_cases.description: Check changed Python services for injection, access control, sensitive data, and unsafe deserialization risks.

use_cases.title: ORM Performance Review
use_cases.description: Inspect SQLAlchemy model and query changes for N+1 queries, missing indexes, and inefficient data loading.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current worktree changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my changed files for security, performance, bugs, and project standards. Summarize the highest priority issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Review Staged Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review before committing staged changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review only my staged files. Prioritize correctness, OWASP Top 10 risks, and SQLAlchemy performance issues.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for sensitive backend changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current diff with a security focus. Check injection, authentication, access control, secret handling, and unsafe parsing.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Backend Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for backend and database changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a deep review of the changed backend files. Include ORM query behavior, transaction risks, edge cases, and standards compliance.

output_examples.input: Review my changed backend files before I commit.
output: Lists reviewed files and groups findings by severity.
Highlights a missing authorization check as a critical issue.
Notes an N+1 query risk and explains the expected database impact.
Suggests specific follow-up tests for the changed behavior.

output_examples.input: Check this SQLAlchemy change for performance problems.
output: Identifies relationship access inside a loop.
Recommends eager loading or a batch query approach.
Explains how the change reduces database round trips.

output_examples.input: Do a security review of the current diff.
output: Checks the diff against OWASP categories.
Flags unsafe user input handling and secret exposure risks.
Separates required fixes from optional maintainability suggestions.

best_practices: Run it from a clean repository state so changed files are easy to identify.
Ask for security, performance, and correctness priorities when time is limited.
Review the suggested fixes before allowing any code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample reference code as production code without local context.
Do not rely on it as a substitute for tests, static analysis, or dependency scanning.
Do not allow automatic edits when you only need review comments.

faq.question: What files does this skill review?
faq.answer: It is designed to review files changed in the current git working tree or recent commits.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No, but its strongest guidance targets Python backend code, SQLAlchemy, and OWASP review patterns.

faq.question: Can it find security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It guides the assistant through common OWASP checks, but findings still need developer validation.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and may suggest tests, but it does not run them by default.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm that any referenced project standards files exist and that edits require your approval.
